summary: The note follows the Spencer family of Charleston, South Carolina, who since September 2023 have revived the Sunday supper tradition, cooking a different family recipe each week for a year. Prompted by the discovery of an old recipe book, the meals become a way to share family stories, learn techniques, experiment with substitutions, and strengthen family ties across generations.
one_line: A Charleston family revives the Sunday supper, cooking a different heirloom recipe weekly for a year to reconnect generations through food and stories.
key_facts: The Spencer family of Charleston, South Carolina has held a weekly Sunday supper since September 2023, with a different family recipe each Sunday.
Marie Spencer, the matriarch, found a dusty, leather-bound recipe book in early September, which led the family to reinstate the Sunday supper tradition.
The family consists of Marie (a retired schoolteacher), her husband Harold (a local carpenter), adult children James and Linda, and youngest child Ellie, who is still in high school.
On October 8th the family served an Irish stew passed down from Harold's great-grandmother, made with lamb and root vegetables.
On November 26th, a traditional macaroni pie became 'Macaroni Pie à la Spencer' using a medley of local cheeses from the farmer's market.
A worn wooden spoon, which James says is as old as their family gatherings, stirred almost every stew and sauce, including the tomato sauce on December 17th's pasta night.
On March 14th the family used herbs and vegetables from Marie's garden: basil for pesto, tomatoes for salads, and peppers for a curry.
Linda struggled at first with homemade pie crust but perfected it, using it for a blueberry pie served on April 6th.
On May 11th, over collard greens and cornbread, Marie shared stories of her parents and the lessons from their kitchen.
On June 22nd the family made a fusion jambalaya combining local shrimp with Asian spices.
Desserts such as bourbon pecan pies and chocolate cakes were prepared the day before each supper; by July 20th a grand-niece introduced vegan options.
Marie explained the commitment was not just about food but about unity and intentionally spending time together.
The Spencers plan to continue the tradition into another September with new favorites added and old staples revisited.
